content.title: Oscars 2026: Michael B. Jordan pulls off historic win
content.text: One Battle After Another took home best picture winner, but a huge award was taken home by Michael B. Jordan, who earned his first Academy Award on Sunday night, winning best actor for his dual performance as twins Smoke and Stack in Ryan Coogler’s Sinners, the blockbuster vampire allegory reframing America’s racial history. It was Jordan’s first nomination — and a breakthrough in a category where only five Black men had previously won. Jordan topped a formidable slate that included Timothée Chalamet, Ethan Hawke, Wagner Moura, and Leonardo DiCaprio, defying early-season odds that had favored Moura and Chalamet. His victory at the Actor Awards earlier this month signaled a late surge, and the Oscars confirmed it. The win adds to Sinners’ growing haul. With 16 nominations, the film is now the most‑nominated title in Academy history. The ceremony also marked a milestone for K‑pop. “Golden,” from KPop Demon Hunters, became the first K‑pop song ever to win both a Grammy and an Oscar. Before their speech was abruptly cut off, Ejae managed to share a brief reflection: “Growing up everyone made fun of me for liking K‑pop. And now everyone is singing our song.” She added that the track isn’t about fame — “it’s about resilience.”What to Know:One Battle After Another and Sinners dominated the ceremony, each collecting top‑tier awards and driving the night’s suspense.Paul Thomas Anderson won best director and adapted screenplay, adding supporting actor, casting, and editing wins to his film’s haul.Ryan Coogler’s Sinners secured four Oscars — original screenplay, best actor, cinematography, and score.Michael B. Jordan became the first performer ever honored for dual roles, playing twins Smoke and Stack.Autumn Durald Arkapaw became the first woman and first Black cinematographer to win the category, asking all the women in the Dolby Theatre to stand during her speech.Anderson used his writing win to address the world his children will inherit, calling for “common sense and decency.”Coogler credited his cast, studio, and family for believing in him.Cassandra Kulukundis won the first‑ever Oscar for casting, upsetting favorite Francine Maisler.Sean Penn won supporting actor for One Battle After Another; Amy Madigan earned supporting actress for Weapons in a late‑career triumph. KPop Demon Hunters won best animated feature, with director Maggie Kang dedicating the win to Koreans worldwide.Frankenstein claimed three awards — costume design, makeup and hairstyling, and production design — aided by a cheeky Devil Wears Prada 2 promo moment from Anne Hathaway and Anna Wintour.The live‑action short category ended in a two‑way tie between Two People Exchanging Saliva and The Singers, prompting an awkward attempt by producers to move things along.Billy Crystal honored Rob Reiner, and Barbra Streisand paid tribute to Robert Redford, underscored by the message, “Art can lead change.”All the Empty Rooms won short doc; Mr. Nobody Against Putin took feature documentary.Conan O’Brien opened with a drag parody of Weapons’ Aunt Gladys, earning a standing ovation.This live blog is now closed. Mar 15, 2026 at 10:45 PM EDT‘One battle after another’ closes out the 98th Oscars with six winsPaul Thomas Anderson’s One Battle After Another ended the night as the dominant force at the 98th Academy Awards, taking home six Oscars, including best picture and best director — a career‑defining sweep that firmly cements Anderson among the most influential filmmakers of his era. His political epic about authoritarianism and civic resistance also claimed trophies for adapted screenplay, supporting actor (Sean Penn), casting, and editing.Ryan Coogler’s Sinners remained close on its heels, finishing with four wins for original screenplay, score, cinematography, and Michael B. Jordan’s historic best actor victory. Jordan’s dual performance as twins Smoke and Stack marked the first time an actor has ever won an Oscar for playing two roles in the same film. He thanked Coogler and Warner Bros. for “betting on original ideas and original artistry.”The night also delivered a landmark behind the camera: Autumn Durald Arkapaw became the first woman — and first Black cinematographer — to win the category, asking every woman in the Dolby Theatre to stand as she dedicated the moment to those who helped her reach it.Anderson used his screenplay speech to strike a political note, telling his children he hoped their generation would bring “common sense and decency” to a world his own had left in disarray. Coogler, accepting his writing award earlier in the night, thanked his cast, collaborators, and family for giving him the confidence to pursue the film.The ceremony also marked the Academy’s first‑ever casting Oscar, awarded to Cassandra Kulukundis for assembling the sprawling ensemble of One Battle After Another, an upset over favorite Francine Maisler (Sinners).Other major moments included Amy Madigan’s late‑career supporting actress win for Weapons, KPop Demon Hunters taking best animated feature, and Frankenstein sweeping three craft categories. Directed by David Borenstein and Pavel Talankin, the film follows Talankin’s work at a school in Karabash, a struggling mining town near the Ural Mountains, where he quietly recorded the state’s expanding demands for “patriotic displays” and government‑approved lessons.Shot over two years, the documentary captures the moment when schools were ordered to upload footage proving compliance with Kremlin messaging — a requirement that gave Talankin cover to film meetings, classroom sessions, and officials without raising suspicion. As surveillance around him intensified, he ultimately fled Russia in 2024 with the help of the filmmakers and international partners.The film premiered at Sundance, winning a Special Jury Award, and went on to claim major honors, including the BAFTA for Best Documentary and the Academy Award for Best Documentary Feature.
